holes_found.description: The PRED-095 card is scored under DR-1 with a gentler standard than the one used to falsify our own B1-M-001 upper band. Both results sit in the same draft, and both lean toward the dome. (a) Different test direction. Our band's upper portion is "FALSIFIED as-if" because there is no DETECTION beyond each station's 3-sigma threshold after the CTL-1 discount (registered_prediction_scorecard.B1-M-001.as_if_DR1). The card instead survives because the observed fit is "not EXCLUDED" from -17.8 nT at 30-60 min lags (1.4-2.9 SD) (prediction_level.PRED_095.card_scored_on_registered_component_H.readings.R3_eclipse_attributable_joint_fit). Under the card's standard, our own upper band at SPT tau 30/60 would NOT be falsified: the observed eclipse-attributable values -9.39/-12.06 nT (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev4-scripts-20261004.json:outputs.rev4_pred095_card.json) lie INSIDE our band beyond the threshold. (b) CTL-1 is applied to one side only. The lagged H fits that rescue the card are the same ones the draft says are reproduced at non-eclipsed, night-side Hermanus (-9.5/-12.0 nT; control_station_check.lagged_H_fit_reproduced_at_HER). For our band, that reproduction removes them as evidence. For the card, they still keep -17.8 "not excluded". The card block itself says they are "not eclipse evidence either way", then uses them anyway. (c) The card's own text restricts timing. Its claim and falsifier both read "during eclipse totality" (03-predictions.txt:1425-1426; verified identical at the pinned SHA c3b9f56 and on the served page). A 30-60 min lagged response is not "during totality". At the lags the text admits (tau 0-15), -17.8 is 4.1-7.7 SD from every fit, with power 1.00 at both stations (outputs.rev4_pred095_card.json R3 rows). (d) The card's own lines are reported without their control-day rates. Its falsifier band is met on 5/19 (EBR) and 9/25 (SPT) ordinary days, and its claim band on 1/19 and 2/25. The headline gives the equivalent numbers for our band ("17 of 30 ordinary days - non-diagnostic"), but not for the card. Net: under one consistent rule the card's -17.8 nT is testable on R3 at admissible lags and absent. That is the same "falsified as-if" status our upper band gets. The card's own falsifier not firing remains a dome-favourable finding, just as our own registered metric being "met" is reported as non-diagnostic. The draft's consequence statements (operator_decisions.decision_5; labels_under_options.if_PRED_095_scores_the_card_recommended.option_A = "pending"; symmetric_labelling_options.option_A.consequences[1]; EXP-687-rev4 newsworthy line) therefore do not follow from the draft's own rules. This is not a review-killer, because the error is generous to the dome. It is a breach of the erratum symmetry obligation, which is the main reason this file exists.
holes_found.recommendation: Pick ONE DR-1 standard and apply it to both sides. Recommended: (i) score both sides on eclipse-attributable fits (R3) with the detection standard and the CTL-1 discount (the standard already used for ours); restrict each registration to the lags its own text admits (card: "during totality" -> tau 0-15, report tau 30 as sensitivity; our band: our frozen +/-60 min window). Result: card "falsified as-if (DR-1; its own falsifier did not fire - disclosed)". (ii) Alternatively, use the consistency standard (claimed value excluded at >= 3 SD) for both. Then re-score our B1-M-001 upper band at SPT/EBR lagged cells, and some cells will become "not excluded". Either way, report the card's R1 literal reading as untestable under DR-1 (control 3-sigma 24-27 nT > 17.8), and add the card's control-day band rates (falsifier 5/19, 9/25; claim 1/19, 2/25) next to ours in the headline. Then rewrite labels_under_options, decision_5's consequence sentence, option_A.consequences[1], both proposed notes and the EXP newsworthy line. Under recommendation (i), decision_5 no longer changes PRED-095's Option-A label: it becomes a representation correction only. That is the better position, because then the choice of registration cannot be read as choosing the outcome.

holes_found.description: The lag-absorption argument is used in one direction only. REV4-JOINT discounts the quadratic-trend rejection of the -10.9 baseline because "the quadratic trend absorbs part of a lagged response" (joint_amplitude_test.result_minus10p9). The same injection table (z_component_evaluation.lag_mismatch_injection) shows that a MISMATCHED template also attenuates, which lowers the expected k under x1.672 as well. The x1.672 rejection, however, is computed as if template and true response always match ("REJECTED ... >= 3.8 ... across all 8 variants"). Reviewer approximation (our_side_recomputations[8]): with the lag-matched template the x1.672 rejection holds at true lags 0-30 min (>= 3.76 plain-SD units, dome coverage) and is 2.89 at lag 60 (tau30, linear). Read literally, the rule's "every variant" falls to 1.24 (tau0|lin vs a 60-min true lag). Separately, tau30|quad is the most lag-robust variant (recovery 0.91-1.00 at lags 15-60), and there k = 1 sits 4.8-7.8 SD away. So "the quadratic trend cannot carry the rejection" is too broad: it holds for tau0|quad, not tau30|quad. The dome's texts bound the admissible lag: the paragraph says "Z minimum within 30 minutes of maximum eclipse coverage" (03-predictions.txt:72-73), Tier 1 says "umbra-locked" (:107) and the card says "during totality". Within those bounds the x1.672 conclusion survives. The draft does not say this, so the result rests on an unstated assumption.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a lag-aware version of the joint test. Inject lagged responses (0/15/30/60 min) at the x1.672 and -10.9 amplitudes into the control days at all 8 stations. Refit k with each template and report the distance from the EXPECTED recovered k, not from 1 or 1.672. State the admissible lag window from the dome's own texts (<= 30 min paragraph; "umbra-locked"; "during totality"), and give the x1.672 result inside it. Correct "every variant" to "every lag-matched variant within the dome's stated timing". Report tau30|quad's lag robustness alongside the -10.9 discussion, both directions. Apply the same attenuation caveat to the per-station power and consistency_z tables (they inject the fitted template itself).

holes_found.description: The headline overstates one station-set result. It says the revised -17 to -21 nT Z prediction "is absent at every station above 80% coverage". That is true on the dome's own coverage table (EBR, SPT; COI has no data). It is not true on the ephemeris >80% set, which the draft reports side by side (prediction_level.PRED_095.paragraph_scored_on_Z.station_sets_side_by_side.ephemeris_gt80_dome_cited). LER (ephemeris 0.88) has a linear-trend Z fit 0.42 SD from its x1.672 amplitude, with power 0.56 (power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes.x1672_per_station.obscuration_tau0_linear.LER; dome_favourable_findings[9]). "Outside the range" holds at 0 of 7, but "absent" (tested with power and not seen) does not hold at LER. In a summary, "absent at every station" reads as the stronger claim.
holes_found.recommendation: Headline: "...is outside its range at every station and excluded with power at every station above 80% coverage on the dome's own table; on our ephemeris coverage, LER (88%) cannot exclude it (power 0.56)." Make the same change to proposed_note_option_A/B ("detectable and absent").

holes_found.description: Standard physics is represented by the best-fitting proxy, and the hnote's sign-geometry request is not met. The headline and kernel say a "solar-elevation weighting - what standard physics expects for a sunset eclipse - fits it better still", and the EXP kernel says standard Sq physics "also produces larger effects where the Sun stood higher". Two standard-physics proxies were fitted. sin(solar elevation) fits well (chi2 2.90 ephemeris / 6.44 dome coverage). The draft's own local Sq-weakening proxy fits WORST of all five profiles in the primary variant (chi2 20.0 vs FSF 3.96 and our binary 11.18; site_registered_tests.WIN_010_profile.result_Z_rev4.alternative_profiles). That second result is disclosed only in position_dependent_sign_check.consequences. Naming the proxy that fits as "what standard physics expects" is the post-hoc model selection we would reject if the dome did it. HNOTE item 1 also asked for the sign geometry (Ashour-Chapman thin sheet / Meza 2022), not a one-signed or local-level proxy. Meza et al. (verified this run, arXiv:2107.12327 section 3.2) report opposite-signed dZ at BOU versus VIC/NEW, which they attribute to "relative location to the eclipse path". The draft's proxy explicitly ignores "current redistribution around the shadow" (sq_proxy), which is that geometry. A path through northern Iberia puts SPT and GUI on one side and CLF/HAD/ESK/LER/NGK on the other. A thin-sheet expectation could therefore itself produce a latitude-ordered Z pattern, and that bears directly on whether the latitude-ordered residual is "standard-physics-shaped". Whether it matches the observed ordering is untested.
holes_found.recommendation: Either compute an Ashour-Chapman thin-sheet expectation (Meza's approximation; conductivity hole scaled by obscuration at about 18:30 UT) for the 8 stations and add it as a profile, or soften every mention to: "one simple standard-physics proxy, sin(solar elevation), fits about as well as FSF; our cruder local Sq proxy fits worst (chi2 20.0) - our representation, not a test of the Sq mechanism; a geometry-aware (Ashour-Chapman) expectation was not computed". State the Sq-proxy misfit as plainly as the binary-profile failure. Change "produces" to "can produce" in both kernels.

holes_found.description: We repeat a dome arithmetic error as if it were correct. two_dome_specifications.arithmetic says "The PRED-095 card does the same in one step: -18.22 x 0.978 x (1 - 0.022) = -17.8 nT". The expression evaluates to -17.43 nT. -17.8 is -18.22 x 0.978 without the (1 - 0.022) factor. The card's centre and its +/-2 band [-19.8, -15.8] are therefore inconsistent with the card's own formula ([-19.43, -15.43]). The scoring outcome does not change (observed R1 -9.6/-12.6 nT and R3 fits lie outside both bands). Still, a frozen-results file should not endorse an arithmetic line it did not check. This is the arithmetic analogue of the C3-1 lesson.
holes_found.recommendation: Rewrite: "The card states -18.22 x 0.978 x (1 - 0.022) = -17.8 nT; the expression evaluates to -17.43 nT (-17.8 omits the (1 - 0.022) factor, which the card does not explain). We score the card's stated -17.8 +/- 2; the band shift does not change any outcome." Add it to dome-internal inconsistencies, not to dome_favourable_findings.

holes_found.description: Archiving the inputs is presented as optional (_meta.data_publication_state; operator_decisions.decision_ots). It should be a precondition for the stamp. The manifest proves WHICH bytes were used. It does not let anyone re-derive the results once BGS GIN replaces the best-available files with quasi-definitive or definitive versions. EBR, CLF, KOU and part of GUI are Variation data, and every 2026 file will be superseded. An OTS stamp over results whose inputs then disappear has the same weakness our Timestamp Error tab criticises: it proves the content existed, not that it can be checked. Size is manageable: about 809 IAGA files (248 + 93 + 468) at about 104 kB, roughly 84 MB raw or about 13 MB gzipped (one EBR day: 104,583 bytes -> 16,359 gzipped). Counter-consideration: INTERMAGNET/BGS redistribution terms must allow republishing raw files on a public site. The repo is public, so this needs checking before commit, not after.
holes_found.recommendation: Make archiving a precondition of the stamp: a gzipped tarball plus manifest under predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-results-inputs/, with the INTERMAGNET acknowledgement and licence text, after confirming the terms. If the terms forbid redistribution, store the archive privately with its sha256 in the stamped file, and say so. Also pre-declare NOW, in the stamped file, the definitive-data re-run rule: re-run when definitive 2026 data are published; publish a dated, separately stamped addendum; treat a result as material only if a label changes or a stated SD distance crosses 3. Declaring this before definitive data exist keeps the re-run from becoming a post-hoc choice. Do NOT wait for definitive data before stamping (likely 2027). Baseline-level differences are mostly absorbed by the per-day trend terms, and a year of "pending" has its own cost.

holes_found.description: The draft uses two conventions for the same "lagged/eclipse-attributable H fit" numbers. registered_prediction_scorecard.B1-M-001.as_if_DR1 (SPT tau30/60 -8.8/-11.3, EBR tau60 -11.4 nT) and dome_favourable_findings[4] / control_station_check (EBR/SPT tau30 -8.5/-8.8) quote the raw fit amplitude A. prediction_level.PRED_095.card_scored_on_registered_component_H uses A - null_mean (SPT -9.39/-12.06, EBR -11.88). Both cite outputs.rev3_fits.json (sha 993bf4fc...), so a reader cross-checking finds two different numbers for one fit.
holes_found.recommendation: Use A - null_mean ("eclipse-attributable") everywhere, or label the raw A explicitly where it is kept for comparison with the HER template fits.

stronger_arguments.description: For decision_5: our own predictions.json PRED-095 entry already carries the CARD's registration date (2026-04-04, not the paragraph's 2026-03-15/03-28) and, apart from a one-character typo, the card's hash prefix. Choosing the card corrects the claim text to match the metadata we already recorded. It is not a new choice made after seeing the data. Say this in decision_5.

The dome's own texts give a timing bound: the paragraph says "within 30 minutes of maximum", Tier 1 says "umbra-locked", the card says "during totality". This bound is both the answer to the lag-mismatch objection (C4-2) and the reason the card's lagged rescue fails (C4-1c). Using the proponent's own timing is stronger than any post-hoc lag choice of ours.

Meza et al. 2022 now passes a direct full-text check (the first citation in this cluster to be verified this way, in two separate reviews: WIN-010.c18 and this one). It can carry the position-dependent-sign point openly instead of being "not re-read; nothing rests on it".

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is right on three points, and the draft credits all three. Eclipses do perturb ground magnetometers: raw H at the dome's stations was 13-19 nT low (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20261004T054500.json:dome_favourable_findings[0]). Its Boulder quiet statistic is well defined: this review re-fetched BOU 2026-08-12 and 2019-07-12 from BGS GIN and reproduced 7.62 and 4.17 nT exactly (our_side_recomputations[0]). The eclipse-window Z residuals do increase northward in FSF order, more than on any of 19 control days (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20261004T054500.json:z_component_evaluation.power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes.joint_amplitude_test.residual). A fourth point, newly in its favour: the PRED-095 card's own falsifier, "H within +/-3 nT of 0 during totality", did not fire on the raw reading (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev4-scripts-20261004.json:outputs.rev4_pred095_card.json, EBR -9.61 / SPT -12.56 nT).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Ordinary days produce the same raw H, and the card's own bands are met on ordinary days (falsifier 5/19 and 9/25, claim 1/19 and 2/25; outputs.rev4_pred095_card.json). On the eclipse-attributable fits at the lags the card's "during totality" admits, -17.8 nT is 4.1-7.7 SD away with power 1.00 (same file, R3 tau 0-15). The latitude ordering appears at about half the -10.9-baseline amplitude and is excluded at the x1.672 amplitude within the dome's own timing bounds (C4-2). FSF is not distinguished from a flat or a solar-elevation profile (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20261004T054500.json:site_registered_tests.WIN_010_profile.result_Z_rev4). A falsifier that does not fire is not a confirmation, just as our own band being "met" on 17 of 30 ordinary days was not.

deeper_analysis: Why C4-1 is major and not minor, even though it favours the dome. The results file's main job, under the stamped erratum, is to apply one rule to both sides. In rev4 our band loses by a detection test plus a control-station discount, and the dome card survives by a consistency test without that discount, at lags its own text excludes. A careful reader will see this, whichever side they are on. The fix is mechanical and makes the decision_5 choice outcome-neutral, which also answers the operator's concern. Other side considered: a defender can say DR-1 is our rule, not the card's, and that "by its own lines" is the only fair reading of a proponent's registration. That is a legitimate position. But then it must be applied to us as well: our B1-M-001 was "met" by its own registered metric, and rev4 overrides that with DR-1. Either reading is defensible. Using one reading for each side is not. On C4-2: the reviewer numbers are an approximation (priority-station mean recovery fractions applied to a joint k). The analyst should run the joint injection directly. The direction of the result is clear: within the dome's stated timing the x1.672 rejection holds, and outside it the rule's "every variant" wording does not. On C4-4: this is not a claim that FSF physics is supported. The residual is about half the formula amplitude and FSF beats flat by only 1.3-3.1 in chi2. The point is that our description of the standard expectation should not be whichever proxy happens to fit. Process note (not a hole in the target): commit 320084e, which added the rev4 artifacts to this repo, carries a commit message from a different project (WIN-010.c18 flagged the same). The content is correct; the message is misattributed.
